premise_review: All eight top-level commands are preserved exactly in raw and organized retained archives; there are three structures and five actual theorem declarations. The archive decision does not deny those proof terms exist.

DiracSpectrumToKTheoryClass takes M : MellKTheory and stores a source, a target, arbitrary mapsSpectrumToKClass/compatibleWithIndex : Prop and supplied proofs. Both first theorems project those proofs without proving any specific relation between source and target.

DiracSpectrumKTheoryFunctor.objectMap is a genuine supplied function from DiracSpectrumObject to KTheoryClass M.K. Its morphismCompatible, preservesIdentity? and preservesComposition? are arbitrary Prop fields with proofs, not formulas about an arrow map or actual functor laws; there is no morphism map.

DiracSpectrumRealizesKTheoryIndex explicitly requires M, I : KTheoryIndex M, bridge and sameClass : bridge.target.value = I.indexClass.value. The final theorem genuinely projects this required equality. The spectralObjectRepresentsIndex proposition is separately arbitrary and its theorem projects the separately supplied witness.

No index/spectrum correspondence, analytic Dirac operator, actual K-theory space, derived category, index theorem, actual functor, naturality, additivity or universal property is constructed. The genuine sameClass equality is retained without upgrading it to any of those claims.

Full captured KTheoryClass/KTheoryIndex/ModuliStackKTheory/CategoricalSpectrum/Tensor context was read. KTheorySpace only stores Base/Class/zero/add/neg/label without group axioms; MellKTheory and index/Dirac relationships are contract-level propositions. These captured sources do not resolve the exact historical environment or establish domain semantics.

No source-body edits, new aliases, namespace rebinding, provider replacement or maintained duplicate contract module is generated. All original notices and descriptive claims remain in exact archives, explicitly bounded by this review.
